LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT 1976

LICENSING OF TRADES, BUSINESSES AND INDUSTRIES (FEDERAL TERRITORY OF

KUALA LUMPUR) BY-LAWS 2016

IN exercise of the power conferred by paragraph 102(s) of the

Local Government Act 1976 [Act 171], the Commissioner of the City of Kuala Lumpur

makes, and pursuant to section 103 of the Act, the Minister confirms, the following

by-laws:

PART I

PRELIMINARY

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These by-laws may be cited as the Licensing of Trades, Businesses and

Industries (Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur) By-Laws 2016.

(2) These By-laws come into operation on 1 September 2016.

Interpretation

2. In these By-laws, unless the context otherwise requires—

"business activity" means any trade, business or industrial activity as specified in

the Schedule;

"Commissioner" means the Commissioner of the City of Kuala Lumpur appointed

under section 4 of the Federal Capital Act 1960 [Act 190];

"licence fee" means the prescribed payment rate for a licence issued under these

By-laws as specified in the Schedule;

"private higher educational institution" shall have the same meaning as defined

in the Private Higher Educational Institutions Act 1996 [Act 555];

"licensee" means any person to whom a business premise licence is issued under

these By-laws for the purpose of operating a business activity as prescribed in the

Schedule;

"premise" shall have the same meaning as defined in the Street, Drainage and

Building Act 1974 [Act 133];

"private health care facilities and services" shall have the same meaning as

defined in the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services 1998 Act [Act 586];

"business premise" means a premise which is used to operate a business

activity; and

"private school" or "private educational institution" shall have the same meaning

as defined in the Education Act 1996 [Act 550].

PART II

LICENSING

Licence required for business activity

3. (1) Any person may use any premise for operating any business activity when

a planning approval, if necessary, for that purpose has been obtained under the

relevant planning law and a business premise license has been issued pertaining to the

said premise by the Commissioner under these By-laws.

(2) Any person who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Application for a licence

4. (1) Subject to by-law 3, an application for a licence under these By-laws shall

be made in such form and manner as determined by the Commissioner.

(2) The Commissioner may approve or not approve an application for a

licence under these By-laws.

(3) The Commissioner may, if he thinks necessary, require any applicant to

attend in person or on behalf of a corporation or firm, or a representative authorised by

the corporation or firm to attend to furnish any document or further information

regarding an application for a licence.

(4) A licence issued under these By-laws shall be subject to—

(a) the licence period as determined by the Commissioner;

(b) the suitability and the size of the premise to be used to operate the

proposed business activity;

(c) the provisions of these By-laws, conditions and restrictions

imposed by the Commissioner and by any relevant authorities;

(d) payment of deposit as provided in by-law 8;

(e) payment of a licence fee as prescribed in the Schedule; and

(f) any other requirements under any relevant laws.

(5) The Commissioner may, from time to time and while a licence is still in

force, impose any additional conditions on the licence or amend or revoke any condition

imposed on the licence.

(6) A written notice shall be given to the licensee before the Commissioner

makes any decision under paragraph (5).

Disqualification

5. Notwithstanding by-law 4, no licence shall be issued under these By-laws to any

person—

(a) under the age of eighteen years old; or

(b) if the premise proposed by him, in the opinion of the

Commissioner, is not suitable to be used as a business premise or

the proposed premise is located in an area which is not suitable for

operating the proposed business activity.

Form of licence

6. A licence issued under these By-laws shall be in any form as may be determined

by the Commissioner.

Licence fee

7. (1) The licence fee payable for the issuance of a licence under these By-laws

is as specified in the Schedule.

(2) The Commissioner may exempt any licensee from the responsibility of

paying the whole or any part of the licence fee.

(3) The licence fee paid under paragraph (1) shall not be refundable.

Deposit

8. (1) The Commissioner may require any person to whom a licence is issued to

pay a deposit of an amount of money not exceeding fifty thousand ringgit to ensure that

the provisions of the Act, By-laws and the conditions or restrictions of the licence are

observed.

(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Commissioner may exempt any

licensee from the responsibility of paying the whole or any part of the deposit.

(3) If there is a breach of any of the provisions of the Act, By-laws, conditions

or restrictions of the licence, the Commissioner shall give notice to the licensee within

the time specified in the notice to give representation as to why his deposit shall not be

forfeited.

(4) The Commissioner may, after considering the representation given by the

licensee or if the licensee fails to make a representation, decides either to forfeit the

whole or part of the deposit.

(5) Subject to paragraph (4), the Commissioner may require the licensee to

replace the whole or part of the deposit that has been forfeited.

(6) The deposit paid shall, unless forfeited, be refunded to the licensee

without any adjustment for interest on the amount deposited under paragraph (1) after

the licensee has ceased operating the business activity.

(7) The licensee shall inform the Commissioner if he has ceased operating the

business activity.

(8) Notwithstanding paragraph (7), the licensee shall apply to the

Commissioner within thirty days from the date he has ceased operating the business

activity for his deposit to be refunded.

(9) If the licensee does not apply for his deposit to be refunded or the deposit

is not claimed within the period specified under paragraph (8), the deposit shall be

forfeited and shall be paid into the fund constituted under the law relating to the local

government and shall form part of the revenue of the fund.

Replacement of licence

9. If the Commissioner is satisfied that a valid licence issued under these By-laws is

lost, defaced or damaged, the Commissioner may issue a replacement licence.

Transfer of licence

10. (1) The licensee may submit an application to transfer the licence to any

party in such form as determined by the Commissioner and the Commissioner may

approve or refuse such application.

(2) The fee for the transfer of the licence shall be fifty ringgit.

(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if there is a change of entity or change of

name in the entity, the licensee shall forward a copy of the certification of the change

from the Companies Commission of Malaysia.

Renewal of licence

11. (1) A licence issued under these By-laws shall not be renewed as a right and

an application for renewal of licence shall be deemed as an application for a licence.

(2) An application for renewal of a licence shall be made within sixty days

before the expiry of the licence and shall be made in such form and manner as may be

determined by the Commissioner.

(3) The Commissioner may, if he thinks necessary, require any applicant to

attend in person or on behalf of a corporation or firm, or a representative authorised by

the corporation or firm to attend to furnish any document or further information

regarding an application to renew a licence.

(4) The Commissioner may renew or not to renew a licence and shall inform

the applicant of his decision in writing or by any other manner as may be determined by

the Commissioner and to refund the deposit to the applicant subject to by-law 8(9).

(5) A licence if renewed under paragraph (4) shall be subject to—

(a) the licence period as determined by the Commissioner;

(b) payment of a licence fee as prescribed in the Schedule; and

(c) the provisions of these By-laws, conditions and restrictions

imposed by the Commissioner and by any relevant authorities.

(6) No further deposit need to be given by the licensee if his licence is

renewed.

(7) The Commissioner shall not be responsible to pay any compensation to

the licensee if the licence is not renewed under paragraph (4).

Revocation of licence

12. (1) The Commissioner may revoke a licence issued under by-law 4 if he is

satistified that—

(a) the licensee has contravened any provisions of the Act, By-laws,

conditions or restrictions of the licence;

(b) the licensee has, either in relation to the application of a licence or

at any time after the licence is issued, submitted to the

Commissioner, a document or declaration which is false, confusing

or not accurate;

(c) the licensee has not operated the licensed business activity for a

consecutive period of three months without informing the

Commissioner; or

(d) a winding up order or bankruptcy order was made against the

licensee or a resolution for voluntary winding up has been

approved.

(2) Revocation of licence under paragraph (1) may be made by the

Commissioner without any payment of compensation to the licensee and the

Commissioner may forfeit the whole deposit paid under by-law 8.

(3) Before the revocation of a licence, the Commissioner shall give a notice in

writing to the licensee requiring him to make a representation within the period as

specified in the notice as to why his licence shall not be revoked.

(4) (a) After the expiry of the period specified in the notice under

paragraph (3) and after considering the licensee's representation or if the licensee fails

to make a representation, the Commissioner shall proceed to consider such matter and

inform his decision in a written notice to the licensee.

(b) If the Commissioner decides to revoke the licence, the revocation

of the licence shall take effect on the date specified in the notice served to the licensee.

(5) Any licensee who operates a business activity after his licence is revoked

under paragraph (4) commits an offence.

PART III

SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR TIMBER STORE

Prohibition of burning of sawdust and timber waste

13. (1) The licensee shall not permit any person to burn sawdust or timber waste

within his timber store area unless permitted by the Commissioner subject to any

conditions as the Commissioner thinks necessary.

(2) The licensee shall ensure that the cut timber in the timber store is stored

and stacked in a tidy or orderly manner to the Commissioner's satisfaction and in such

manner that does not obstruct an entrance, exit or passageway.

(3) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) or (2) commits an offence.

PART IV

SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR LAUNDRY

Definition

14. For the purpose of this Part, unless the context otherwise requires—

"laundry" means any business premise providing service for washing or ironing

of clothes commercially, either manually, mechanically, using steam, dry cleaning or in

any other manner; and

"clothes" includes clothing, towels, linen, rugs, cushion covers, table cloths,

blankets, pillow covers, bedsheets, curtains or any other washable items made from

woven material.

Wall and floor specifications

15. (1) The walls of the laundry where washing is done manually shall be fixed

with glazed tiles or water resistant material to a height of not less than two metres

unless exempted by the Commissioner.

(2) The floor of the laundry where washing is carried out shall be made of

smooth impervious material and graded so that all fluids are flowing and not stagnant in

the wash area.

(3) Any laundry licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) or (2) commits an

offence.

Special requirements for laundry

16. (1) The laundry licensee shall ensure that—

(a) washed clothes are separated from dirty clothes and shall be kept

on shelves, tables, in containers, or in a suitable storage;

(b) all utensils, equipments, fittings and machinery in his business

premise be kept in a clean condition at all times; and

(c) washed clothes are not to be dried on the ground and shall be

dried on clothes lines or at a specific place for drying clothes

within his business premise area.

(2) Any laundry licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Prohibition of lending out clothes

17. (1) No laundry licensee shall use, lend or hire out any clothes entrusted to

him to be washed or ironed.

(2) Any laundry licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

PART V

SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR BEAUTY AND HEALTH CARE CENTRE

Definition

18. For the purpose of this Part, unless the context otherwise requires—

"cosmetic" means any substance used for treating or maintaining the

complexion, skin or hair and includes toiletries;

"hairdressing'' means hair removal or transplant, haircutting, hairwaving,

trimming, dyeing, shaving, shampooing and every similar operation usually performed

by a hairdresser either manually, mechanically, electrically or by means of any powder

or solution or by any combination of such methods;

"beauty and health care centre" means—

(i) any business premise used to provide beauty treatment or health care but

does not include a hospital or a clinic where patients are treated under

the supervision of a medical practitioner registered under the

Medical Act 1971 [Act 50], an infirmary, a nursing or convalescent home

or any other similar premises providing the following services or any

combination of the following services:

(a) facial treatment;

(b) manicure and pedicure;

(c) waxing;

(d) hairdressing;

(e) tattoo;

(f) application of cosmetics or beautifying;

(g) body slimming;

(h) herbs, milk or flower bath;

(i) body scrub; or

(j) any other activities as may be determined by the Commissioner as

beauty and health care treatment.

(ii) any business premise used to provide massage, physical fitness treatment

or exercise with or without equipment providing the following services or

any combination of the following services:

(1) massage:

(a) traditional massage;

(b) handicapped massage;

(c) reflexology;

(d) aromatherapy;

(e) modern massage using any equipments;

(f) physiotherapy;

(g) acupuncture; or

(h) bekam;

(2) sauna, spa and jacuzzi;

(3) aerobics, fitness centre or gymnasium;

(4) meditation centre; or

(5) any other health treatment permitted by the Commissioner;

"treatment" means any beauty treatment, facial treatment, manicure and

pedicure, hairdressing, steam bath or any other special bath, chiropody, electrical

treatment, body slimming or any other similar treatment or physical fitness exercise

with or without equipment;

"herbal remedy" means any treatment using herbal substances or a mixture of

herbal substances produced by the process of drying, crushing or comminuting, but

without involving any other process, a natural substance or substances of plant or

mineral origin or any other parts of such substance or substances; and

"beauty treatment" means any treatment by application of cosmetics or herbal

remedy on the body or any part of the body, face or hair for treating or improving the

complexion of the body or face, body slimming, facial massage, hairdressing, manicure

and pedicure, sauna or herbal bath and spa but does not include any form of plastic

surgery.

Prohibition on full partitioning of beauty and health care centre

19. (1) The licensee shall not fully partition or permit to be fully partitioned the

space or use tinted glass in the business premise used for beauty and health care centre.

(2) The licensee may, in the space used for beauty treatment, use a curtain or

screen made of any material determined by the Commissioner to separate the beds used

for providing beauty treatment but such curtain or screen shall not exceed two metres

in height from the floor.

(3) The surface of door of the area where beauty treatment is rendered shall

be one-fourth covered by transparent glass and the door shall be kept unfastened

during the business hours.

(4) Any licensee who contravenes this by-law commits an offence.

PART VI

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Prohibitions

20. (1) No licensee shall—

(a) employ any person who is under the age of eighteen years;

(b) employ any foreigner without a valid work permit to work in his

business premise;

(c) allow any gambling or immoral activities or allow any conduct

which will cause nuisance, disturbance, injury or noisiness to the

residents within the surrounding area of his business premise;

(d) allow any animal to remain in his business premise other than the

premise operating a business or providing a service relating to

animal; and

(e) operate other activities in his business premise other than the

business activity specified in his licence.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Medical examination

21. (1) The Commissioner may at any time, if he thinks necessary, instruct the

licensee and his employees to undergo a medical examination by a medical or health

officer registered under the Medical Act 1971 [Act 50].

(2) Any licensee who fails to comply with the instruction issued under

paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Register of employees

22. (1) The licensee shall provide a register book containing the name, identity

card number, passport number and a valid work permit of non-citizen employees,

recent residential address, qualification, photograph and any other relevant particulars

of his employees and shall produce the register book for inspection whenever required

by the Commissioner.

(2) Any licensee who fails to comply with paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Sanitary requirements and maintenance of the business premise

23. (1) The licensee shall—

(a) ensure that all mechanical or electrical equipment which is used in

his business premise is maintained in a good condition and safe to

be used at all times;

(b) keep all areas, forecourts and open spaces forming part of his

business premise to be in a clean condition;

(c) provide sufficient refuse bins in his business premise; and

(d) provide sufficient toilet facilities and ensure that the toilet is in a

clean condition at all times.

(2) Any licensee who fails to comply with paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Disposal of refuse

24. All refuse related to the business activity shall be placed in plastic bags or any

other suitable containers before being deposited into refuse bins or receptacles and

shall be disposed of in such manner as may be determined by the Commissioner or by

any agency responsible for such matter.

Spilling of noxious liquid or refuse

25. (1) No licensee shall cause any noxious liquid or refuse relating to his

business activity to be thrown, discarded, spilled, left or scattered in any public place.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

(3) For the purpose of this by-law, "public place" shall have the meaning as

defined in section 2 of the Local Government Act 1976 [Act 171].

Ventilation and lighting

26. (1) The licensee shall ensure that—

(a) there is sufficient and suitable lighting in his business premise;

(b) there is sufficient ventilation in his business premise; and

(c) every staircase, passage, exit and emergency exit forming part of

his business premise is provided with sufficient lighting.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Crowded space is prohibited

27. (1) The licensee shall ensure that his business premise is not crowded with

any furniture, things or goods relating to his business activity which may affect the

safety, health or in a situation that may cause nuisance to any person in the business

premise.

(2) If in the opinion of the Commissioner, a business premise is in a crowded

situation, the Commissioner may by notice in writing direct the licensee within the

period specified in the notice to rearrange the furniture, things or goods within the

business premise until the Commissioner is satisfied that the business premise is no

longer in a crowded situation.

(3) Any licensee who fails to comply with the notice issued under

paragraph (2) commits an offence.

(4) Notwitstanding paragraph (3), any licensee who fails to comply with

paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Firefighting equipment, staircases, exits and doors

28. (1) The licensee shall ensure that—

(a) there is sufficient firefighting equipment approved by the relevant

authorities installed in his business premise and in a working

condition; and

(b) all staircases, passages, landings and exits if forming part of the

business premise are maintained in good order and clear from

obstruction and every door in the business premise is constructed

and fitted as to be readily opened at all times.

(2) The Commissioner may, by notice in writing instruct the licensee to carry

out the requirements under paragraph (1) within the period specified in the notice.

(3) Any licensee who fails to comply with the notice issued under

paragraph (2) commits an offence.

(4) Notwitstanding paragraph (3), any licensee who contravenes

paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Inflammable substances

29. (1) Cement or any inflammable solution shall be kept in closed containers of

approved design by the Commissioner.

(2) Where solvents, solutions or cement having a flash point below 23ºC are

kept in quantities exceeding 45 litres, a non-flammable store shall be constructed

according to the requirements of the Commissioner.

(3) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) or (2) commits an offence.

Storage

30. (1) All materials shall be stored in such manner and state as to prevent the

emission of noxious or offensive effluent therefrom.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Burning

31. (1) The licensee shall not burn or cause to be burnt refuse or materials or

other waste in relation to his business activity except in such manner and at a place

approved by the Commissioner.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Effluent

32. (1) The licensee shall not discharge or cause or permit to be discharged any

effluent except scheduled effluent which complies with the limit of discharge as

prescribed under the Environmental Quality (Sewage) Regulations 2009

[P.U. (A) 432/2009] and the Environmental Quality (Control of Pollution From Solid

Waste Transfer Station and Landfill) Regulations 2009 [P.U. (A) 433/2009], at a place or

places as specified by the Commissioner to discharge effluent and approved in writing

by the Director General of the Department of Environment.

(2) For the purpose of paragraph (1), "effluent" shall have the meaning given

to it under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 [Act 127] and regulations made

thereunder.

Spreading of dust, etc.

33. (1) The licensee shall not cause, let, allow or permit any spreading of dust,

fume, vapour, gas heat, radiation, odour, smell, vibration, smoke or soot from his

business premise which in the opinion of the Commissioner is a nuisance or which may

cause air pollution.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Nuisance

34. (1) The licensee shall not, during the operation of his business activity in the

business premise, create or cause or allow any nuisance to occur.

(2) Any licensee who contravenes paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Operating hours for business activity

35. (1) The Commissioner may direct a business activity to be operated in the

business premise within the period and time as specified by the Commissioner and the

licensee shall comply with such direction.

(2) The Commissioner may consider an application from the licensee to

extend the period and time specified by the Commissioner under paragraph (1) upon

receiving an application in writing from the licensee.

(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), any licensee who contravenes

paragraph (1) commits an offence.

Power to enter premise for inspection purposes

36. The Commissioner may—

(a) enter and inspect any business premise used or which the Commissioner

suspects with reasonable cause is being used to operate any business

activity for which a licence is required under these By-laws; or

(b) request from the licensee any information regarding the management of

the business premise and the licensee or his employee shall provide any

information required from him.

Exemption

37. The Commissioner may, conditionally or unconditionally, exempt any licensee

from any provision of these By-laws.

Penalty

38. Any person who contravenes any provision of these By-laws, shall be guilty of an

offence and shall, on conviction, be liable to a fine not exceeding two thousand ringgit or

to imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year or to both, and in the case of a

continuing offence, to a fine not exceeding two hundred ringgit for each day during

which the offence is continued after conviction.

Revocation and transitional provisions

39. (1) The following By-laws are revoked:

(a) The Barber Shops and Hairdressers (Federal Territory)

By-Laws 1979 [P.U. (A) 8/1980];

(b) the Timber Store and Woodworking (Federal Territory)

By-Laws 1981 [P.U. (A) 236/1981];

(c) the Laundrette (Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur)

By-Laws 1985 [P.U (A) 291/1985];

(d) the Licensing of Trades, Businesses and Industries

(Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur) By-Laws 1986

[P.U (A) 408/1986]; and

(e) the Beauty and Health Establishment (Federal Territory of

Kuala Lumpur) By-Laws 2003 [P.U. (A) 22/2003].

(2) Any licence issued or approval granted under the revoked By-laws before

the coming into operation of these By-laws shall continue in full force until the licence

expires, is amended, suspended or cancelled, or the approval expires or is revoked

under the By-laws, for which purpose only the revoked By-laws shall continue to be in

full force and effect.

(3) Any proceeding pending or commenced under the revoked By-laws

before the coming into operation of these By-laws shall be continued and concluded

under the revoked By-laws as if these By-laws had not been made.
